A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPLAVU study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched reliably despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original privacy–utility comparisons, gender-bias evaluations, ablations, gait-recognition results and appendix experiments on scaling and efficiency.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds video-level privacy comparisons, inversion attacks, video retrieval and qualitative reconstruction experiments.

M1.justification: The frozen encoder, self-attention AAM, three training objectives and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedure. The explicit CLS/average-pooled embedding description clarifies implementation; the added evaluations do not establish a revised SPLAVU algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds VP-HMDB51 and VP-UCF101 evaluation using five clip-level private attributes, alongside the retained VISPR and PA-HMDB51 evaluations. It also adds UCF101 action-video retrieval and feature-inversion/video-reconstruction scenarios, substantially broadening task requirements and threat coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 2 evaluates a supervised latent anonymizer trained with private-attribute labels against SPLAVU. This differs from the existing pixel-level VITA comparator. Table 8 also adds random-chance references; the original Table 1 comparator roster remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols specify learned black-box inversion and gradient-based white-box inversion, assessed with predictors trained on raw features. Reconstruction compares four token-input conditions with 10-epoch decoder finetuning; retrieval uses test queries, a training-set gallery and Recall@1/5/10 plus mAP. These are substantial protocol additions, while retained experiments keep their settings.

E4.justification: The original task, loss, architecture and sensitivity ablations remain. v2 adds a substantial security analysis: Table 8 tests embedding recoverability under black-box and white-box attacks, while Figure 4 compares reconstruction from patch and CLS representations with and without anonymization.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run error bars. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged after matching renumbered tables. New results include SPLAVU privacy cMAP of 70.5/69.6 versus raw-feature 76.4/75.9 on VP-HMDB51/VP-UCF101 (Table 2), inversion outcomes (Table 8), UCF101 retrieval R@1 of 94.9 versus baseline 95.3 (Table 13), and qualitative reconstruction findings (Figure 4).

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and reasoning remain substantively unchanged. Equation (1), dataset symbols and loss-weight naming receive notation cleanup; Appendix B.1 explains standard global-token and pooling representations without introducing a new theoretical argument or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about latent anonymization, multi-task generalization, approximately 35% privacy-leakage reduction and gender-bias mitigation. The additional experiments support or qualify these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges failure against white-box inversion and interprets the tested black-box attack as leaving attribute prediction near chance. It newly restricts current applicability to global-embedding tasks, leaving patch-based tasks for future work, and discusses spatial-information loss in reconstruction. These materially expand the earlier limitations and interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies CLS versus globally pooled encoder outputs, and the new experiments document decoder and retrieval setup details. Existing training hyperparameters and project-page access remain unchanged. Removing 'linear' from the privacy-evaluation prose reconciles it with the two-layer MLP already documented in both appendices.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations on video representations, bias and safety, including Swetha et al. (2021, 2023), Prabhu and Birhane (2020), SAFE-LLaVA and SAFER-CLIP. The central positioning against pixel-level anonymization and the claimed novelty of generalizable latent anonymization remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained. Changes include a new embedding-notation subsection, localized explanatory additions, standardized dataset notation, wording corrections and updated affiliations and conference headers; there is no extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2, 8 and 13 and the reconstruction panels in Figure 4, and expands Figure 2’s caption. Existing diagrams, plots and table designs remain substantially intact; the original runtime Figure 4 becomes Figure 5, with local relocation and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct inversion and reconstruction tests of its central privacy claim. v2 substantially strengthens assessment through these tests, explicit disclosure of white-box vulnerability, clearer applicability limits, clip-level privacy comparisons and held-out retrieval evaluation. The gains concern evidence and transparency rather than higher retained scores. Reconstruction evidence still has limits: non-anonymized CLS inputs also reconstruct poorly, so Figure 4 cannot attribute all resistance to AAM.
